blocks.content: As there are numerous excellent texts on matrix algebra, we made little effort to prove most of the results given below. For statistical applications, concise introductions can be found in the chapters on matrix methods in Johnson and Wichern (1988) and Morrison (1976), while Dhrymes (1978) and Searle (1982) provided more extended treatments. Wilf's (1978) short chapter on matrix methods provides a very nifty review of methods useful in applied mathematics. Franklin (1968), Horn and Johnson (1985), and Gantmacher (1960), respectively, presented increasingly sophisticated treatments of matrix analysis.
